groups.passage:
Howler monkeys are named for the long loud cries, or howls, that they make every day. They are the loudest land animal and their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests. Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory. Everyone starts and ends the day by howling to check out where their nearest competitors are.
Interestingly, when there are few howler monkeys in an area, the howling routine takes on a different pattern. In Belize, where howler monkeys were newly reintroduced into a wildlife sanctuary, the howler monkeys were heard only a few times a week rather than every day. Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors. At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild. In the future when the population grows, there will be no need for the recording because the howler monkeys will have more reason to check in with the neighbors to define their own territories.

groups.passage: After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads. Eventually, the demand for a road across the mountains led to the building of the Going-to-the-Sun Road. The construction of the Going-to-the-Sun Road was a huge task. After 11 years of work, the final section of the road was completed in 1932. The road is considered an engineering feat. Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built. It is one of the most scenic roads in North America. The construction of the road has changed the way visitors experience the Glacier National Park. Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see. Just across the border, in Canada, is the Waterton Lakes National Park. In 1931, members of the Rotary Clubs of Alberta and Montana suggested joining the two parks as a symbol of peace and friendship between the two countries. In 1932, the United States and Canadian governments renamed the parks the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, the world’s first. More recently, the parks have received several international honors. They were named as a World Heritage Site in 1995. This international recognition highlights the importance of this area, not just to the United States and Canada, but to the entire world.

groups.passage:
Ice sculpting is a difficult process. First, ice must be carefully selected so that it is suitable for sculpting. Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity. It should also have the minimum amount of air bubbles. Perfectly clear ice blocks weighing 140 kg and measuring 100 cm × 50 cm × 25 cm are available from the Clinebell Company in Colorado. Much larger clear blocks are produced in Europe and Canada or harvested from a frozen river in Sweden. These large ice blocks are used for large ice sculpting events and for building ice hotels.
Another difficulty in the process of ice sculpting is time control. The temperature of the environment affects how quickly the piece must be completed to avoid the effects of melting. If the sculpting does not take place in a cold environment, then the sculptor must work quickly to finish his piece. The tools used for sculpting also affect when the task can be accomplished. Some sculptures can be completed in as little as ten minutes if power tools are used. Ice sculptors also use razor-sharp chisels that are specifically designed for cutting ice. The best ice chisels are made in Japan, a country that, along with China, has a long tradition of magnificent ice sculptures.
Ice sculptures are used as decorations in some cuisines, especially in Asia. When holding a dinner party, some large restaurants or hotels will use an ice sculpture to decorate the table. For example, in a wedding banquet it is common to see a pair of ice-sculpted swans that represent the union of the new couple.

groups.passage:
If you touch your finger to a hot stove, you know it’s going to hurt. However, if you convince yourself beforehand that the pain won’t be so bad, you might not suffer as much. According to a recent study, the part of your brain that reacts to severe pain is largely the same part that reacts to expectation of pain.
Researchers in this study worked with 10 volunteers, ages 24 to 46. Each volunteer wore a device that gave out 20-second-long pulses of heat to the right leg. There were three levels of heat, producing mild, moderate, or strong pain. During training, the volunteers would first hear a tone, followed by a period of silence, and then feel a heat pulse. They then learned to associate the length of the silent pause with the intensity of the upcoming heat pulse. The longer the pause, the stronger the heat pulse would be, causing more severe pain.
A day or two later, the real experiment began. The researchers found that the parts of the brain involved in learning, memory, emotion, and touch became more active as the volunteers expected higher levels of pain. These were mainly the same areas that became active when participants actually felt pain. Interestingly, when the volunteers expected only mild or moderate pain but experienced severe pain, they reported feeling 28 percent less pain than when they expected severe pain and actually got it.
The new study emphasizes that pain has both physical and psychological elements. Understanding how pain works in the mind and brain could eventually give doctors tools for helping people cope with painful medical treatments.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: We should learn to be sensitive to pain.
options.B: Our feeling of pain is decided by our environment.
options.C: How people feel pain remains unknown to scientists.
options.D: Our reaction to pain is closely related to our expectation of pain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the pulses of heat in the study?

options.A: Each heat pulse lasted for 20 seconds.
options.B: The pulses were given to the arms of the volunteers.
options.C: Different devices gave out different levels of heat pulses.
options.D: There were two levels of heat intensity given to the volunteers.

questions.stem: How did the volunteers learn to expect different levels of heat?

options.A: From the loudness of the tone they heard.
options.B: From the instruction given to them by the researchers.
options.C: From the color of a light flashing on the device they wore.
options.D: From the length of the pause between a tone and the heat pulse.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what may be the author’s advice to a doctor before a surgery?

options.A: To provide the patient with more pain killers.
options.B: To talk to the patient and ease his/her worries.
options.C: To give the patient strong heat pulses beforehand.
options.D: To emphasize the possible severe pain to the patient.

sections.title: 二、英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長120個單詞(words)左右。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示︰你（英文名字必須假設為George或Mary）向朋友（英文名字必須假設為Adam或Eve）借了一件相當珍貴的物品，但不慎遺失，一時又買不到替代品。請寫一封信，第一段說明物品遺失的經過，第二段則表達歉意並提出可能的解決方案。
請注意：為避免評分困擾，請使用上述提示的George或Mary在信末署名，不得使用自己真實的中文或英文姓名。
questions.scoring_notes:
評分標準：
本大題總分 20 分，主要評量考生是否有能力撰寫一篇語法正確、語意通順，並且內容統一、組織連貫的英文作文。採整體式評分，分為五等級：特優（19-20 分）、優（15-18 分）、可（10-14 分）、差（5-9 分）、劣（0-4 分），閱卷委員於閱讀完考生試卷後，於腦海裡產生一個整體（holistic）分數，再以分項式評分標準檢閱是否符合整體印象分數，分項式評分指標包含下列 5 項：內容（5 分）、組織（5 分）、文法、句構（4 分）、字彙、拼字（4 分），及體例（2 分）（詳見表 1）。另外，字數不足，扣 1 分；未分兩段在體例部分，扣 1 分；未使用適當書信格式（如未書寫稱呼語及信末署名），扣 1 分。
表 1：英文作文分項式評分指標
項目＼等級｜優｜可｜差｜劣
內容｜優：主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4 分)｜可：主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3 分)｜差：主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1 分)｜劣：文不對題或沒寫(凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算)。(0 分)
組織｜優：重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4 分)｜可：重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3 分)｜差：重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1 分)｜劣：全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0 分)
文法、句構｜優：全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4 分)｜可：文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3 分)｜差：文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1 分)｜劣：全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0 分)
字彙、拼字｜優：用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4 分)｜可：字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3 分)｜差：用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1 分)｜劣：只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0 分)
體例｜優、可（合併一格）：格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2 分)｜差：格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1 分)｜劣：違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0 分)
註2：改編自張武昌等（民 93）「英文寫作能力測驗規劃研究（VI）」研究報告。台北：大考中心。95 年學測在「項目」部份再行修改、定稿。

tags.topic: apologizing to a friend for losing a valuable borrowed item and proposing solutions

extraction.method: 題本：python-docx 讀 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx）為主，與 pdftotext -layout paper-1.pdf 逐段比對，並用 Read 看題本第 2–8 頁影像確認空格位置與版面；答案：pdftotext answer.pdf；評分原則：pdftotext scoring.pdf + Read 看第 4–6 頁影像（翻譯參考答案與作文評分表為圖片，人工轉寫）；統計：xlrd 讀 stats-1（P/Ph/Pl/D）、stats-2（選項分析 T 列）、stats-3（非選擇題分數分布），並程式核對選項分析的星號選項與官方答案一致、答案選項選答率等於答對率 P
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 94–110 期別一致：詞彙 1–15（各1分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，各1分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，各1分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，各2分）、翻譯題 2題×4分、英文作文 20分；選擇題 72 分＋非選擇題 28 分＝100 分。
翻譯題與作文的題號：題本第貳部分翻譯題印「1.」「2.」，作文沒有題號；為避免與選擇題 1、2 重複（validator 要求 no 為整數、label 不可重複），no 依序編為 57、58、59（非題本題號），label 用「翻譯1」「翻譯2」「作文」。

翻譯參考答案在 scoring.pdf 第 5 頁是大括弧排列的圖片（依原註 1「{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞；( )（括弧）表示該字詞可省略」）。翻譯1 各大括弧互不相依，填 answer_segments：({which/that}) 寫成 [which / that / 空字串]，all (of) your life. 與 (for) a lifetime. 展開為 all of your life.／all your life.／for a lifetime.／a lifetime.，加上 your whole life.／for life.，共 54 種；answer 原為帶大括號記號的轉寫，改為各段第一個寫法串接的完整句子 “Listening to music is a hobby which you can enjoy all of your life.”，answer_is_composite: true。翻譯2 有兩種句型（「OR」之後是 But if you can play …），主詞與動詞部分結構不同，改填 answer_variants 39 句（35 句取自大括弧圖；另 4 句依評分說明「連接詞 But/Yet/However 為首的句子」把句首 But 換成 Yet／However,）；answer 改為 “But being able to play a musical instrument can give you even more joy.”（第一種句型各括弧取第一個寫法），answer_is_composite: true；原本的兩種大括號轉寫（{ } 內以「 / 」分隔可互換的字詞，( ) 表示可省略）依序放在 accepted_answers，scoring_notes 末尾加解析註說明。
scoring.pdf 中重抄的題目文字與題本略有出入（翻譯說明作「請將以下兩個中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意的英文」；作文提示作「第一段說明遺失的經過」），JSON 的 instructions／stem 一律以題本為準。
非選擇題統計（stats-3.xls）只有大題層級的分數人數分布（第一題＝翻譯題兩小題合計，滿分 8；第二題＝作文，滿分 20），放在 s5、s6 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義的延伸欄位，percent 已換成 0–1 小數），小題 stats 為 null。

選擇題 stats：correct_rate＝P、high_group＝Ph（前33%）、low_group＝Pl（後33%）、discrimination＝D（stats-1.xls）；option_rates 取 stats-2.xls 選項分析的 T（全體）列，原表為整數百分比，加總因四捨五入不一定等於 1，未答比例（0–2%）未收錄。已程式核對每題選項分析標星號的選項與 answer.pdf 一致，且該選項比例等於 P。
題本各題組前的「41-44 為題組」「45-48 為題組」等標示未放入 passage（題組範圍可由 questions 題號得知）。
第 27 題所在選文的「Romanic」（建築風格通常稱 Romanesque）照題本原文保留，非抽取錯誤。
paper-2.doc 的翻譯題標題「一、」與兩句前的「1.」「2.」是 Word 自動編號，轉 docx 後遺失；標題依 PDF 題本寫為「一、翻譯題(8%)」。docx 與 pdftotext 的其餘文字逐詞比對一致。
作文題目中英文名字前後的空白：Word 原檔為「假設為George或Mary」（無空白），PDF 排版顯示有間距，stem 依 Word 原檔文字。

查證（verifier）：56 題答案逐題對照 answer.pdf（含影像）全部一致；每題題幹、選項、選文、文意選填選項庫與 paper-2.doc（docx）逐字比對、與 pdftotext paper-1.pdf 逐詞比對（含 [[題號]] 空格位置）全部一致；8 篇選文段落數與字數一致；56 題 stats（P/Ph/Pl/D 與 T 列選項比例）全部對照 stats-1、stats-2 一致，s5、s6 分數分布對照 stats-3 一致；翻譯參考答案與作文評分表對照 scoring.pdf 第 5–6 頁放大影像一致。題本無任何圖表（pdfimages 無圖片）。

翻譯題 scoring_notes：scoring.pdf 原文為同一段說明兩句（「第一句主要在於…；而第二句在測驗…」），兩小題各取與本題相關的部分；第58題補回原文的「而」字（原解析漏抄）。作文 scoring_notes 的表 1 為圖片表格，逐列轉寫為「項目｜優：…｜可：…｜差：…｜劣：…」，表頭寫成「項目＼等級｜優｜可｜差｜劣」（已移除原解析自行加上的「（等級：優／可／差／劣）」說明文字）；「體例」列的優、可兩欄在原表合併為一格。註1、註2 為原文腳注。
